sources.title: IRGC says it struck two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that were escorted by U.S. military
sources.snippet: IRGC said it struck two oil tankers attempting to transit the strait via routes unauthorized by Iran, forcing several other ships to turn around; the ships were under U.S. Central Command air escort. CENTCOM has struck Iranian air defence, command/control, coastal radar, anti-ship missile capability and 60+ IRGC small boats in and near the strait.

sources.title: Strait of Hormuz Brief: 29 July, 2026
sources.snippet: Preliminary data show 39 transits during 20-26 July, down from 82 the previous week; single-day transits fell to 10 vs. an ~88/day pre-crisis run-rate. Non-Iranian-linked traffic fell 27% w/w, hit hardest, down to 17 from 53 transits.

sources.title: Update 072 to JMIC Advisory Note
sources.snippet: Threat level for the Strait of Hormuz raised to SUBSTANTIAL; mine risk persists with clearance ongoing; over 30 maritime incidents reported across the Arabian Gulf, Hormuz and Gulf of Oman since 28 February with no consistent flag-state targeting pattern; merchant traffic severely constrained by EMI/AIS/GNSS interference.

sources.title: IMF PortWatch: Strait of Hormuz transit tracking
sources.snippet: Daily transit-call and volume tracking for the Strait of Hormuz; recorded 10 transits on 23 July against a pre-crisis baseline of 88/day, corroborating the sharp collapse in traffic reported by Lloyd's List.

sources.title: Middle East shipping insurance costs rise on Hormuz risks: Marsh
sources.snippet: Marsh's global head of marine, cargo and logistics said additional war-risk premiums rose from 1-3% of hull value several weeks earlier to a current 7.5-10%; underwriters increasingly unwilling to offer spot terms after IMO recorded eight ships hit 13-20 July.

sources.title: LNG disputes emerge after disruption at Ras Laffan, Strait of Hormuz: Key considerations
sources.snippet: Legal/commercial analysis of force majeure and charter-party disputes following the Ras Laffan missile strikes and Hormuz transit disruption, confirming QatarEnergy's force majeure declaration and its knock-on effect on LNG offtake contracts.

sources.title: IEA Member Countries agree to new emergency oil stock release in response to market turmoil
sources.snippet: 32 IEA member countries unanimously agreed to release 400 million barrels from emergency reserves, the largest coordinated release in IEA history, in response to the Middle East war; Asia-Oceania stocks available immediately, Americas/Europe from end-March.

sources.title: Ras Laffan attacks could reshape global LNG supply as outage timeline extends
sources.snippet: Iranian missile strikes on 18-19 March damaged two LNG trains and a GTL facility at Ras Laffan, cutting roughly 17% of Qatar's LNG export capacity, with part of the complex facing a 3-5 year repair window.

sources.title: الحرس الثوري يعلن اعتراض 3 ناقلات نفط في مضيق هرمز
sources.snippet: IRGC navy announced it hit and detained three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on the morning of 29 July, saying the vessels were sailing an unsafe/unauthorized route despite prior warnings; a targeted Qatari-linked tanker was named. IRGC reiterates the strait is closed until U.S. 'hostile acts' end.

sources.title: Treasury Warns of Sanctions Risks Linked to China-Based Independent "Teapot" Oil Refineries
sources.snippet: Treasury warned financial institutions of sanctions exposure from dealings with independent Chinese refineries importing Iranian crude, part of an intensified enforcement push against the teapot-refinery channel that handles most of Iran's ~90%-to-China export flow.

sources.title: Gulf shipping cover still available as premiums hit 10%
sources.snippet: Despite reduced underwriter willingness to write spot terms at 7.5-10% of hull value, aggregate global war-risk hull capacity ($2.5bn-$3bn) remains well above the exposure of Gulf-transiting tankers (mostly under $100m each), so cover has not been formally withdrawn.

sources.title: Yanbu gives Aramco limited option for rerouting crude
sources.snippet: Yanbu's nominal loading capacity of ~4.5mn b/d (1.5mn North, 3mn South) is a hard bottleneck versus the East-West pipeline's 7mn b/d capacity; February 2026 LSEG data showed Yanbu South exporting only ~1.1mn b/d, near its historical baseline, implying limited unused headroom versus the pipeline's nameplate.

sources.title: How shipping insurance rates are rising, as Hormuz, Bab al-Mandeb shut down
sources.snippet: Confirms the same July premium surge (war-risk into double digits of hull value) alongside compounding Bab al-Mandeb risk, framing the Gulf and Red Sea as jointly stressed chokepoints for war-risk underwriting.

sources.title: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
sources.snippet: Consolidated timeline: crisis began 28 Feb 2026 with US/Israeli strikes and Khamenei's assassination; IRGC forbade Hormuz passage, boarded/attacked ships and laid mines; an 8 April Pakistan-mediated ceasefire lasted two weeks before IRGC re-restricted passage 19 April; by end-July, conflict is in its 140th+ day with no ceasefire and the Islamabad MOU declared void by both sides.

sources.title: OPEC+ approves fourth oil output quota hike since Hormuz closure
sources.snippet: OPEC+ core members raised output quotas by ~600,000 b/d cumulatively April-June, but actual group production fell to 33.19mn b/d in April from 42.77mn in February because Gulf members' physical exports are constrained by the strait itself, not by policy — quota headroom cannot be shipped.

sources.title: US sanctions China's teapot refinery for buying Iranian oil
sources.snippet: US Treasury sanctioned a Shandong-based independent refinery for purchasing over $1bn of Iranian crude, including oil linked to IRGC-Qods Force front companies; China's Commerce Ministry issued a blocking-statute style rejection of the sanctions.

sources.title: Behind Iran's War Chest, an Oil 'Lifeline' from China
sources.snippet: Sanctions-research analysis tracing how shadow-fleet tankers and teapot refinery buying continue to fund Iran's war effort despite enforcement escalation, and flags Kharg lifting data (Kpler) falling from ~1.4mn b/d in February to ~0.32mn b/d by mid-April as Kharg nears storage capacity.

sources.title: 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
sources.snippet: Background on the US Fifth Fleet-led blockade posture against Iranian shipping, distinct from and in tension with IRGC's own claimed closure of the strait to US/Israeli-linked traffic.

sources.title: CENTCOM Launches Retaliatory Attack on Iran (7 July 2026)
sources.snippet: Military-affairs blog detailing CENTCOM's early-July retaliatory strikes on Iranian coastal military infrastructure, corroborating the CENTCOM target list (radar, C2, anti-ship missiles, small boats) later cited in the 31 July Washington Times report.

sources.title: Strait of Hormuz Closed, Day 153 | Live Tracker & Monitor
sources.snippet: Independent live tracker: strait effectively closed since the 28 Feb 2026 declaration (day 153 as of late July); notes 8 major container carriers suspended Hormuz transits/rerouted via Cape of Good Hope and war-risk running at ~8x normal.

sources.title: OPEC+ countries say they will expand monthly oil production
sources.snippet: Reports OPEC+'s announced production expansion as largely symbolic given Gulf members' Hormuz-side export constraints; largely republishes the same quota-hike fact set as the CNBC coverage.

sources.title: Strait of Hormuz Oil Supply Shock: The 2026 Crisis Explained
sources.snippet: Cites Vitol CEO Russell Hardy's assessment that essentially all of the world's spare oil production capacity (Saudi + UAE) sits geographically behind the strait, so the closure blocks not just current flow but also the reserve buffer markets rely on.

sources.title: US warns banks of sanctions risk over China 'teapot' refineries handling Iranian oil
sources.snippet: Follow-on coverage of the same Treasury teapot-refinery warning, noting Iranian barrels are frequently relabeled as Malaysian-blend crude to obscure origin before reaching Chinese buyers.

sources.title: Widespread GPS Jamming Hits 1,000-plus Ships in the Middle East
sources.snippet: Maritime-analytics vendor blog quantifying GPS/AIS jamming affecting 1,100+ vessels in a 24-hour period, with ships erroneously placed at airports, a nuclear plant, and on land across Iran, Oman and the UAE.

sources.title: Aramco announces first quarter 2026 results
sources.snippet: Confirms East-West (Petroline) pipeline operating at its 7mn b/d maximum capacity in Q1 2026; standing operator disclosure on bypass-route utilization, not a new event.

sources.title: Murban Reporting
sources.snippet: ADNOC's own rolling Murban export-availability forecast page; confirms the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline's 1.5mn b/d maximum discharge capacity as the ceiling on UAE's Hormuz-bypass throughput. Standing operator data, not a new event.

sources.title: Oil - Port of Fujairah
sources.snippet: Confirms FOTT storage capacity of ~1.18mn cubic metres and Fujairah's role as one of the world's three largest bunkering hubs, the key staging point for Hormuz-bypass diversion. Standing infrastructure disclosure.

sources.title: Habshan-Fujairah oil pipeline
sources.snippet: Background reference on the ~406km ADNOC pipeline linking Habshan onshore collection to the Fujairah export terminal, corroborating the 1.5mn b/d capacity figure from ADNOC's own reporting.
